title: 紫碧山房正宇 Zibi Shanfang zhengyu
subtitle: Yuanming Yuan

model.line: On the block drawn on the Qing plan S01: position and frontage from the plan, heights and roof from the typology of its hall class, its form drawn by the hall kit. It will be updated as the research goes on.
rows: platform 0.45 m, eave 3.2 m, ridge 5.25 m above the ground
gable 硬山 or 悬山, rolled ridge 卷棚, grey tile

by the hall kit: 3 bays, the middle widest, a porch front, steps on the front, 硬山 flush gable with a rolled ridge 卷棚, grey tile, a painted beam under the eave. Drawn from the typology of its hall class, not from a picture of this hall (assumed, C).

evidence.title: 日下舊聞考 紫碧山房
evidence.excerpt_zh: 鴻慈永祜後垣西北為紫碧山房前宇為横雲堂山房東巖洞中為石帆室東南為豐樂軒北為霽華樓迤東為景暉樓横雲堂西池上為澄素樓西北為引溪亭（圎圓明園册）臣等謹按紫碧山房額有二其一恭懸正宇内一懸穿堂門檐與引溪亭額皆世宗御書紫碧山房正宇檐額曰樂在人和及横雲堂諸額皆皇上御書
evidence.summary: North-west beyond the rear wall of 鴻慈永祜: 紫碧山房 with 横雲堂, the cave room 石帆室, 豐樂軒, 霽華樓, 景暉樓, 澄素樓 on the pond and 引溪亭.

evidence.title: 紫碧山房 正宇: 乐在人和
evidence.excerpt_zh: 紫碧山房正宇檐額曰樂在人和
evidence.summary: The plan label 乐?人和 is the plaque on the main hall of 紫碧山房. The same words hang inside 澹怀堂 of 长春园 (j83:3a): that is another hall.

evidence.title: 紫碧山房: 乾隆二十六年 poem of the Qianlong Emperor
evidence.date: 乾隆二十六年 (1761), date from the compilation
evidence.locator: p.195 item (1), under 紫碧山房
evidence.excerpt_zh: 山房卜筑已多年，云构恒瞻圣藻悬。卓尔仰怀仁者乐，佳哉常契画中禅。赵家粉本饶仙趣，陶氏清辞无俗縁。最爱夕阳西下际，鹤林高致会当前。
evidence.summary: Poem of the Qianlong Emperor at 紫碧山房, 1761. Year as given by the compilation.

evidence.title: 紫碧山房
evidence.locator: v3 p.123, under 紫碧山房; source ref 8-749
evidence.excerpt_zh: 因迥为高本不艰，远奇近概献谁悭。康功北郭桑麻里，爽气西山襟袖间。诗意乘空每有会，画家缩地此为闲。是真佳处宜常坐，坐便思回奈少闲。
evidence.summary: Poem 紫碧山房 by the Qianlong Emperor, 1764, filed by the editors under 紫碧山房.

evidence.title: 紫碧山房: 乾隆二十九年 poem of the Qianlong Emperor
evidence.date: 乾隆二十九年 (1764), date from the compilation
evidence.locator: p.195 item (2), under 紫碧山房
evidence.excerpt_zh: 因迥为高本不艰，远竒近概献谁悭。康功北郭桑麻里，爽气西山襟袖间。诗意乘空每有会，画家缩地此为闲。是真佳处宜常坐，坐便思回奈少闲。
evidence.summary: Poem of the Qianlong Emperor at 紫碧山房, 1764, on the view. Year as given by the compilation.

evidence.title: 紫碧山房: 咸丰五年 poem of the Xianfeng Emperor
evidence.date: 咸丰五年 (1855), date from the compilation
evidence.locator: p.196 item (11), under 紫碧山房
evidence.excerpt_zh: 楼高始觉太虚宽，无限诗情结古欢。此日登临供点笔，何人酩酊倩扶冠。千峯从翠澄秋宇，一雁摇空送早寒。处处茅檐真乐意，豳风图画坐中看。雅集山庄礼数宽，惊人老句寄遥欢。凭将往代忠兼讽，好励今时衣与冠。玉岭鸦翻余落日，纸窗虫啮透轻寒。归桡沿路撷芳便，篱菊高低镜里看。
evidence.summary: Poem of the Xianfeng Emperor at 紫碧山房, 1855, on the view. Year as given by the compilation.

evidence.title: 紫碧山房歌(1-130)
evidence.locator: v3 p.133, under 紫碧山房
evidence.excerpt_zh: 御园西北山势雄，回蹊叠石磴道崇。高岩低涧相映带，曲廊幽室连珠栊。峰顶翼然一亭子，旷览周原开百里。灵境题额仰宪皇，智水仁山本至理。登临几暇非遨游，待泽情殷阅绿畴。举头只有天在上，愿鉴微忱宵旰忧。
evidence.summary: Poem 紫碧山房歌(1-130) by the Jiaqing Emperor, 1796, filed by the editors under 紫碧山房.

evidence.title: 圆明园百景史事分景汇编: 紫碧山房
evidence.locator: from p.195, under 紫碧山房
evidence.summary: The compiler calls it the highest point of the garden, called also 寒山, enlarged in 1760 after the Second Southern Tour, in imitation of Suzhou's 寒山. 紫碧山房: 11 dated items, 1761-1855, of which 11 poems (Qianlong, Jiaqing, Daoguang, Xianfeng); recurring themes: the view. First dated 1761, last dated 1855.

evidence.title: 圆明园五朝御制诗文集注 v3, editors' note on 紫碧山房
evidence.summary: Enlarged about 1760: inner gate, 含余清, the octagonal 翼翠亭, 丰乐轩, 纳翠轩, the boat-shaped 石帆室, the three-storey 景晖楼, 横云堂, a five-bay main hall 乐在人和, 澄素楼, 霁华楼. After 1860 the inner gate, main hall and 顺木天 pavilion survived under guard and were lost around 1900, say the editors.

evidence.title: 圆明园百景史事分景汇编: 紫碧山房
evidence.locator: from p.194, under 紫碧山房
evidence.summary: The compiler calls it the highest point of the garden, called also 寒山, enlarged in 1760 after the Second Southern Tour, in imitation of Suzhou's 寒山. 紫碧山房: short note in the compilation, no dated items.

evidence.title: 紫碧山房 2017, 新京报 via 中新网
evidence.summary: 紫碧山房 Zibi Shanfang, the highest point of the garden in the far north-west, yielded a service house, gate, the halls 紫碧山房, 含余清 and 澄素楼, a landing, stone bridge, walls, roads, channel and hill. Remains absent from the documents also appeared: an earlier wall footing with its apron, a retaining wall of the hill, a semicircular landing, a drain and a stone path.

searched: No picture of it found in the Forty Scenes album, its 1745 woodcuts, the Bertin gouaches and the 1887 lithograph; the 20 Xiyang Lou plates; ruin photographs on Commons, at Östasiatiska museet, the Slovene Ethnographic Museum, Historical Photographs of China, the Rijksmuseum, Wellcome and in NDL's albums of about 1900; today's photographs on Commons.
